content:
Eli: Quick question — we need per-tier canaries scoped by region + fallback that doesn't bleed to other tiers. Right now smart routing + global fallback is making enterprise traffic hit v2 and then drop into v1 for hosted users. How do we scope a canary so only enterprise in eu-west gets v2?

Priya: We don't have a single toggle for that today. Routing policies are per-route, fallback chains are global. So if v2 is offered and then fails, fallback can kick in for any route that was routed to v2. That causes the bleed.

Jordan: Proposal: extend rollout config with a scope object. Example:
```yaml
rollout: 
  id: canary-2026-03-17
  variants:
    - name: variant-v2
      weight: 10
    - name: variant-v1
      weight: 90
  scope:
    tiers: ["enterprise"]
    regions: ["eu-west-1"]
fallbackChain:
  - variant-v2
  - variant-v1
  - cpu-fallback
priority: 100
```
This means weights apply only to requests matching scope. FallbackChain stays but we attach a boundary so fallback from v2 -> v1 only resolves within same scope unless explicitly allowed.

Eli: If weights are local to scope that's ideal. Two questions: 1) if enterprise pool saturates and we fallback to hosted pool, do we keep scope semantics? 2) how do we represent that in the API/console so product can see which customers were affected?

Sam: Telemetry-wise we need per-scope metrics: requests, p50/p95 latency, error_rate, fallback_reasons, cost_per_token. Console should show a breakdown: scope -> variant -> fallback histogram. Without that it's opaque.

Marta: On the capacity side: we need a routing priority and compatibility tags. Example: dedicated-pool has tag `dedicated:true, tier:enterprise`. Routing rules should include compatibility and a fallback target list like `fallback_targets: ["enterprise-hosted-compatible","shared-hosted"]`. If dedicated fills up, we attempt `enterprise-hosted-compatible` before global v1.

Jordan: We could encode that with numeric priority and a fallback scope flag. Pseudocode:
```json
{
  "routePolicy": {
    "priority": 50,
    "scopeEnforced": true,
    "fallbackTargets": ["same-tier-hosted", "global-hosted"]
  }
}
```
If `scopeEnforced` is true, fallbacks won't cross tier boundaries unless a policy explicitly permits it.

Eli: UX note: console needs to let you pick (a) scope (tiers, regions, routes), (b) local weight sliders, (c) an explicit "allow cross-tier fallback" checkbox with a warning. Also show an estimated traffic sample and cost delta before enabling.

Sam: I'll add telemetry widgets: per-scope variant heatmap, fallback-reason bar, and a time series for cross-tier fallback count. Will wire to existing per-route traces.

Priya: Also quotas. Canary traffic should count against the scope's committed capacity (reserved pools) not the global. Otherwise enterprise customers might exceed commitments during canary. We need per-scope quota enforcement + alerts.

Marta: Edge case: A/B inside scope where variant-v2 uses more tokens — if scope quota is strict, a 10% canary could blow budget. Console should show estimated quota consumption and optionally enforce a cap.

Jordan: Action items I propose:
- design API extension for rollout.scope + scopeEnforced fallback (PR: #req-420)
- console mockups for scoped canary UI (Priya + Eli)
- telemetry widgets for scope metrics (Sam)
- routing priority and compatibility tags implementation (Marta)
- small load test harness that simulates capacity failover and asserts fallback stays in-scope (Jordan)

deploy-bot: deploy canary: variant-v2 -> eu-west-1 (enterprise) started @ 1723456820, weight: 10% :rocket:

Eli: Perfect. Let's keep scopeEnforced default = true for safety, and require an explicit opt-in to allow cross-tier fallback. Can we track that opt-in in audit logs?

Priya: Yes — audit + rollout change history. We'll also add a "why was traffic routed" debug view per request showing route decision and fallback resolution.

Sam: I'll attach the first set of widgets to the internal dashboard and link them from the rollout page.

Marta: I'll prototype compatibility tags + fallbackTargets next week.

Jordan: I'll open the API PR with tests and a small simulation harness.

Eli: Thanks everyone :thumbsup: This should fix the bleed and make canaries safer for enterprise customers.
